WVPL Blue Bell branch temporarily closing and relocating

Blue Bell , Whitpain Township | Local News

September 17th, 2026 | By Suzanne McNaughton

Discover more
Photo
Library
Lease Commercial Space
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:19
Instaread

The Blue Bell branch of the Wissahickon Valley Public Library (WVPL) will be closed from October 1 through October 19 while staff prepare for renovations. The library will reopen in a temporary location at 960 C Harvest Drive in Blue Bell on October 20. The library is expected to remain there for at least six months while work occurs.

Below is a photo of the entrance to the library’s temporary location and directions to it from the original site:


Photo – WVPL Blue Bell Branch

Photo – Google Maps

Any new holds should be sent the Ambler branch of the WVPL, or to any MCLINC library to be picked up. As for existing holds that have already been assigned for pickup at the Blue Bell library, they will still be sent to Blue Bell and will be available according to the normal hold process. For more information, visit the library’s web page here: https://www.wvpl.org/main-library-renovation-updates-information.

The original library will undergo many improvements during this time, including a roof replacement, repaved parking lot, updated sewer system and creation of new indoor study spaces. View this link to learn more: Library in Blue Bell to make temporary home in nearby office building while undergoing renovation – Around Ambler.

    Women’s Center of Montgomery County to hold 50th anniversary gala

    Fort Washington | Events , Local News

    September 17th, 2026 | By Suzanne McNaughton

    The Women’s Center of Montgomery County, an organization centered on eliminating domestic violence, is celebrating its 50th anniversary on Thursday, October 15. The organization will hold a cocktail gala bringing together advocates, volunteers, organization founders and community leaders. The event will be held at The Highlands Mansion and Estate in Fort Washington at 7001 Sheaff Lane, and will last from 6 to 8 p.m.

    Attendees will hear from keynote speaker Katie Koestner, an advocate for survivors of sexual violence. The gala also features the screening of a trailer for a documentary on the Women’s Center. The documentary is produced by Melissa Davey, a local filmmaker and producer. Tickets for the event are $150 per person and can be found here: 50th Anniversary Gala Celebration – Women’s Center of Montgomery County.

    Founded in 1976, the Women’s Center was originally meant to provide job counseling and health services for women. However, shortly after launching, volunteers found that most of the calls they received were from domestic abuse victims seeking help. Since then, the organization has shifted its focus to preventing domestic violence and all forms of abuse.

    Today, the Montgomery County Women’s Center offers counseling services, shelter, legal assistance, support groups and a 24-hour anonymous hotline from all of its four offices. The organization also provides community education on ways to avoid and identify domestic violence. The Montgomery County Women’s Center has partnered with hospitals, courts, schools and police departments to connect survivors with needed resources. Despite being a women’s center, the organization provides support for anyone facing any abuse. To learn more, visit their website here: Home – Women’s Center of Montgomery County

    Though the center has helped over 200,000 survivors, domestic violence is an ongoing issue. According to the organization, one in three women and one in four men experience some form of abuse from a partner. To contact the Women’s Center of Montgomery County’s abuse hotline, call this number: 1-800-773-2424.

    Happy Chuseok Fest 2026 comes to Blue Bell

    Share
    Blue Bell , Whitpain Township | Events , Local News

    September 17th, 2026 | By Suzanne McNaughton

    The Happy Chuseok Fest, an annual celebration of the Korean Chuseok holiday, is coming to Montgomery County Community College on Saturday, September 19. Hosted by the Korean Culture Community Foundation (KCCF) in collaboration with Montgomery County, the event features food, educational activities and cultural performances from over 15 performing arts groups. Admission is free and open to all ages.

    Chuseok is a Korean harvest festival, often referred to as the “Korean Thanksgiving.” The holiday focuses on gratitude, family, respect and cultural heritage. Chuseok is traditionally celebrated on the fifteenth day of the lunar month, and spans three days in total. During this time, people give thanks for their blessings, pay respects to ancestors and visit and feast with family.

    The Chuseok Fest will offer a K-Culture Experience Village with 10 immersive activities. The event also features Korean foods, informational exhibits, K-Pop music and Taekwondo demonstrations. At 2 p.m., visitors can hear a keynote speech from sociologist Dr. Sam Richards on the importance and history of Chuseok.

    “Happy Chuseok Fest is more than a celebration of Korean culture,” said president of the KCCF, Sharon Hartz. “It is an invitation to our neighbors to experience the meaning of Chuseok together – to share gratitude, discover one another’s cultures, and build a stronger sense of belonging in the community we all call home.” 

    The event will last from 11 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. For more information, visit this link: Happy Chuseok Fest 2026, Montgomery County Community College, Blue Bell, 19 September 2026 | AllEvents.
